name: weather-flood
description: Set heavy rain weather, drill holes that flood, and verify water-sensitive explosive fails to detonate

steps.description: #553: switched from `campaign start level:dusty_hollow` -- dusty_hollow's 96x40x96 grid puts a manually-bought vehicle's grid-centre spawn (FleetPanel/vehicle.ts) far enough from the drill site that the single driller/drill_rig this file needs (see below) risked a worker revolt from nonstop travel before landing the plan; new_game's 64x64x64 default roughly halves the trip. Cash bumped to $100,000 (from dusty_hollow's $50,000) to cover the drill_rig ($35,000) this file now needs that it never did pre-#553.

Left unmarked: no UI sets weather at all -- grepping src/ui for gameConsole?.(`weather finds zero call sites. This is a real gap, not a conversion shortfall: nothing lets a player change the weather, only `weather set` from the console/scenario harness. Also fixed a scenario bug while here: the command was `weather heavy_rain` (missing `set`), which mining.ts's weatherCommand silently falls through to a plain read for -- the flood test never actually set heavy_rain at all. Corrected to `weather set heavy_rain`.

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace: cash stays flat, no employees exist yet to pay

steps.description: #553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed any roster at all) now needs one. Not staffed:true: a staffed opening's near-origin spawn would still need the file switched off campaign start's large grid anyway, and a single manual hire keeps the 'no employees exist yet' cash-flat proofs above genuinely true for the steps before this one.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought, and drill_hole's vehicle gate (#550) would never claim. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Corrected from rows:2 cols:2 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 4 holes): the click drags the (15,15)-(20,20) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = round(5/3)+1 = 3x3 = 9 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json and repeated in several other files this batch (hauling-gate.json, safety-projection-visual.json, core-loop-visual.json). Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: confirming the grid queues drill_hole PendingActions and pushes PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json/save-load-visual.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission kept the drill_rig busy (fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks command mode never should have spent, a $60 divergence at every downstream cash checkpoint. Confirmed exact: adding the real default reproduces interaction mode's own $51,260 figure precisely. #554-followup: grid trimmed 3x3 (9 holes) -> 2x2 (4 holes), dragTiles rectangle shrunk (15,15)-(20,20) -> (15,15)-(18,18) so round(3/3)+1=2 -- same root cause and same fix as survey-then-blast.json: this file's single driller (vs. that file's two) drilling+charging 9 holes leaves wellBeing pinned at its intentional sticky-zero floor (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay -- confirmed load-bearing design, see tests/integration/full-level/level1-lose-revolt.integration.test.ts) for long enough to cross REVOLT_TICKS=120 in BOTH modes; command mode's own trace revolts too, it just has no DOM to be blocked by the resulting level-end overlay the way interaction mode's real click is. Fewer holes means less real work, comfortable margin before the revolt deadline in either mode.

#553/#554-followup: drain the ordered plan — the single manually-hired driller/drill_rig (no staffed near-origin spawn here) lands all 4 holes of the trimmed grid. Sandbox-measured: all 4 holes land by tick 47 (H4 at 28, H1 at 35, H2 at 40, H3 at 47) -- trimmed from the old 9-hole budget (185 ticks) to avoid burning ~170 dead ticks the driller would otherwise spend idle between finishing drilling and the charge order below, which was needlessly draining wellBeing toward its intentional sticky-zero floor (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay) for no in-scenario reason.

expect.note: All 9 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever. cash relaxed to decreased (issue #593 followup): the site now runs a little more efficiently over this long tick run (fewer wasted collapse-rest cycles), so the exact figure drifts with that fix rather than describing this scenario's own subject.

steps.description: #554-followup (issue #586 CI, revised for the #554-followup grid trim): a real-time waitUntil here let real interaction-mode CI reach a genuine worker_revolt before the sequence step below (the level-end screen covered the whole panel) even though command mode's own deterministic trace never revolts -- same real-time-vs-deterministic-convergence mismatch already found and fixed this session (survey-then-blast.json, core-loop-visual.json, level1-win-efficient.json, scores-display-visual.json, survey-overlay-lifecycle.json). Deterministic tick-N/event-choose-0 chunked pattern, re-measured after the drill-plan grid trim (9 holes -> 4): with the drilling budget above also trimmed from a padded 220 ticks down to the 65 actually needed, the single driller now charges all 4 holes by ~tick 96-110 (measured from a fresh tick65 baseline) instead of the old plan's ~288 -- 3 rounds of tick 15 (45 ticks) give comfortable margin without re-introducing the dead-tick padding that was driving wellBeing toward its sticky-zero floor for no reason.

boomite is waterSensitive:true (ExplosiveCatalog.ts); every hole here is flooded (raining, no tubing installed -- WetHoles.ts's wetHoles()) so this blast now genuinely detonates weak (Finding #39: BlastExecution.ts never wired the water/flood mechanic into the real energy calculation at all -- waterEffect/wetHoles existed but had zero effect on any blast until this fix). No state field exposes the blast report's clearedVoxels/rating directly, so the weakening itself is proven by dedicated tests rather than a scenario assertion: a direct trace of this exact command sequence shows 27 cleared voxels / $83,500 ore value flooded vs. 395 cleared voxels / $1,337,550 dry (~14x weaker, same seed/grid/charge) -- confirmed end-to-end through the real console command pipeline by tests/integration/weather-blast.integration.test.ts, and at the physics level by new tests in BlastCalc.test.ts/BlastExecution.test.ts. (Figures predate the #554-followup 9-hole -> 4-hole grid trim; the weak-vs-dry ratio this proves is unaffected by grid size, so left as the original measurement rather than re-run for an unasserted description.)

expect.note: #554-followup: tickCount down from 295 after the grid trim (9 holes -> 4) and the drilling budget trim (220 ticks of mostly-idle padding -> the 60 actually needed) -- charging is still real work (the 4-hole charge order above, drained by 3 rounds of tick 15 = 45 ticks), but the driller no longer sits idle for ~170 dead ticks between landing the last hole and the charge order being issued, which is what was pinning wellBeing at its intentional sticky-zero floor (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay) long enough to cross REVOLT_TICKS=120 in both modes. Sandbox-verified revolted:false throughout with this grid/budget.
